title: Initial Evaluation of Antibody-conjugates Modified with Viral-derived Peptides for Increasing Cellular Accumulation and Improving Tumor Targeting
protocol: In a 1.7 mL microcentrifuge tube, prepare a 10 mg/mL (~1 mg total antibody) solution of mAb 7G3 in PBS, pH 7.6.
Dissolve sulfo-SMCC in DMSO at a concentration of 5-10 mM.
Add the dissolved sulfo-SMCC solution to the tube containing 7G3.
Incubate at room temperature for 1 hour.
Purify and concentrate maleimide-derivatized 7G3 using an ultrafiltration device with buffer exchange in PBS, pH 7.0.
Centrifuge at 8,000 x g for approximately 5 min.
Discard flow through and fill the tube with PBS, pH 7.0.
Centrifuge again.
Perform buffer exchange by centrifuging the protein sample 7-8 times.
Place the filter device upside down in a clean microcentrifuge tube and centrifuge for 2 min at 1,000 x g.
Incubate maleimide-activated 7G3 with 2-fold molar excess of ChAcNLS relative to sulfo-SMCC-to-7G3 ratio used previously overnight at 4 °C.
Monitor the tube during incubation for signs of precipitation and adjust peptide design if necessary.
Concentrate the 7G3-ChAcNLS using an ultrafiltration device in PBS pH 7.4.
Exchange buffer to desired concentration by concentrating the 7G3-ChAcNLS solution.
Perform SDS-PAGE using a 12% polyacrylamide gel.
Mix 10 μg of 7G3-ChAcNLS with PAGE loading buffer containing 2 μL β-mercaptoethanol.
Load the mixture into the well of the gel.
Set the voltage to 120 V and run electrophoresis for 1 hour.
Stop the electrophoresis when the Coomassie dye front reaches the bottom of the gel.
Rinse the gel with destaining solution containing 10% v/v glacial acetic acid and 20% v/v methanol.
Take a photo of the gel.
Measure the distance migrated for the standards and 7G3 conjugates in cm.
Calculate the retention factor (Rf) value by dividing the distance migrated by the gel length.
Plot the molecular weight (MW) in log against the Rf values from each protein standard.
Extrapolate the size of the 7G3 conjugates.
Calculate the number of peptides per antibody by dividing the difference in MW between 7G3 conjugates and unmodified 7G3 by 1768.5 g/mol (MW of ChAcNLS).
Take digital images of the Coomassie-stained gel.
Perform densitometry analysis.
Test the cell selectivity of intracellular accumulation of the peptide-modified mAbs.
Treat target TF-1a cells with 200 nM of 7G3-ChAcNLS including modified control mAbs.
Incubate 5 x 10^6 antigen-positive cells with the conjugates for 1 h at 37 °C.
After 1 hour, remove the supernatant.
Wash cells three times in ice-cold PBS.
Add fresh media and incubate for an additional hour at 37°C.
Remove the supernatant after the additional hour.
Wash cells three times in ice-cold PBS.
Add 0.5 mL of PBS containing 0.25% trypsin and EDTA to cells at 37°C for up to 30 minutes.
Neutralize trypsin with 1.5 mL of cell culture RPMI 1640 media/10% fetal bovine serum.
Centrifuge cells at 500 x g for 5 minutes, then remove supernatant.
Wash cells three times in ice-cold PBS.
Fix cells in 0.5 mL PBS containing 1% paraformaldehyde and 1% sucrose on ice for 30 minutes.
Wash cells three times in ice-cold PBS.
Permeabilize cells in 0.5 mL PBS containing 0.15% Triton X-100 for 5 minutes on ice.
Wash cells in ice-cold PBS and repeat centrifugation.
Suspend cells in 0.1 mL PBS containing 2 μg/mL of an anti-murine (isotype specific) Fc secondary polyclonal antibody conjugated to AlexaFluor 647.
Incubate the suspension for 1 h at room temperature in the dark.
Centrifuge the cells at 250 x g for 5 min.
Wash cells 3 times in 0.5 mL ice-cold PBS.
Suspend cells in 0.5 mL PBS.
Add propidium iodide to a concentration of 10 μg/mL to the cell suspension.
Mount 1 x 10^5 cells onto glass slides using mounting media and cover with a glass coverslip.
Examine cells with a Plan Apo 60X oil immersion objective NA 1.42 on an inverted laser scanning confocal microscope.
Detect propidium iodide fluorescence using the 488 nm argon laser and the spectral scanning prism set for 600 - 650 nm.
For AlexaFluor 647 fluorescence, use the 633 nm helium-neon laser and the spectral scanning prism set for 650 - 700 nm.
Collect fluorescence emissions from propidium iodide and AlexaFluor 647 sequentially.
Use microscope software to acquire images.
Collect images using serial horizontal optical sections of 1,024 x 1,024 pixels with 2X line averaging taken at 0.5 μm intervals through the entire cell thickness.
Present the images as stacked z-projections from four consecutive slices at the maximum fluorescence intensity.
Analyze cells with microscope software.
Record the cellular distribution pattern of the conjugates.
Evaluate whether intracellular fluorescence in the cytoplasm is grouped and near the cell surface or diffuse and homogeneous.
Evaluate the relative fluorescence intensity per cell.
React NOTA-NHS with A14 in 0.1 M sodium bicarbonate at pH 8.6 for 1 hour at room temperature.
Purify and buffer-exchange NOTA-A14 using an ultrafiltration device in PBS, pH 7.6.
React NOTA-A14-ChAcNLS with 100 MBq of 64CuCl2 in 0.1 M sodium bicarbonate, pH 5.5 for 1 hour at 37°C.
Concentrate 64Cu-A14-ChAcNLS in PBS pH 7.4 using an ultrafiltration device to the desired concentration.
Determine the radiolabeling efficiency of 64Cu-A14-ChAcNLS by instant thin-layer chromatography (ITLC).
Apply 0.5 μL aliquot of the reaction solution to the ITLC strip.
Perform an autoradiograph of the ITLC strip and obtain a digital image.
Perform densitometry to obtain the proportion of bound and free 64Cu.
If free 64Cu content is > 5%, return to previous step and perform additional purification.
Perform SDS-PAGE with Coomassie staining to evaluate aggregations.
Perform a second SDS-PAGE followed by an autoradiograph of the gel to determine if there are radiolabeled aggregate species.
Incubate 64Cu-A14 conjugates at increasing concentrations (0-100 nM) in duplicate with 1 x 10^6 target cells per mL.
Mix duplicate samples of 64Cu-A14 conjugates with cells in the presence of 100-fold molar excess of unlabeled A14 to estimate nonspecific binding.
Incubate cell mixtures on ice for 1 hour.
Wash cells after incubation.
Count total bound antibody samples and total nonspecific bound antibody samples in a gamma counter.
Graph specific binding (total bound antibody - nonspecific bound antibody) against reactive free 64Cu-A14 (nM).
Determine the dissociation constant (Kd) by nonlinear regression using graphing software.
Treat cells with 100 nM of the 64Cu-labeled A14 conjugates for 1 h, 6 h, and 24 h at 37 °C.
Include additional parameters such as treatment in the presence of unmodified A14 to block IL-5Rα sites and at 4 °C to block receptor-mediated internalization.
At defined time points, add 0.5 mL of PBS containing 0.25% trypsin and EDTA at 37 °C followed by neutralization and washing.
Incubate cells in plasma membrane lysis buffer on ice for 10 min.
Centrifuge the plasma membrane-lysed cells at 90 x g for 5 min.
Remove supernatant and place in fresh tube.
Wash nuclei 3 times in ice-cold PBS.
Add washes to the cytoplasmic fraction.
Seal vials containing nuclear and cytoplasmic fractions.
Place sealed vials in a gamma counter calibrated for 64Cu.
Perform Western blot analysis for Lamin A/C on whole cell lysate, nuclear, and cytoplasmic fractions.
Perform Western blot analysis for Rab7 on whole cell lysate, nuclear, and cytoplasmic fractions.
Treat 5 x 10^6 cells with 500 μL of radio-immunoprecipitation assay (RIPA) buffer in step 3.12 containing 1%, 2%, and 4% NP-40.
Treat isolated nuclei in 500 μL of RIPA buffer to obtain nuclear proteins.
Precipitate isolated nuclear, cytoplasmic, and whole cell proteins using 4 times the sample volume of cold acetone for 60 min at -20 °C.
Centrifuge precipitated samples at 13,000 x g for 10 min.
Carefully decant supernatant without dislodging protein pellet.
Add 100 μL of PBS to dissolve proteins.
Load 10 μg of protein into each well of a 10% SDS-PAGE gel.
Perform electrophoresis as described in steps 1.7-1.9.
Transfer proteins from gel onto membrane for Western blot analysis.
Identify ladder markers that best correspond to a MW of ~40 kDa.
Cut the membrane in half at this marker.
Probe the blot containing the higher MW proteins with Lamin A/C-specific antibodies.
Probe the membrane with the lower MW proteins with the Rab 7-specific antibodies.
Inject 20-30 μg (6-9 MBq) of 64Cu-A14-ChAcNLS, 64Cu-A14-NLS, and 64Cu-A14 into the tail vein of NOD/SCID mice.
Place a cylindrical phantom containing 5 MBq of 64Cu to convert radioactive counts per second into injected dose per gram of tissue (%ID/g).
Wait 48 hours before anesthetizing mice.
Place mice in an induction chamber with a 1.5 L/min flow of oxygen and 2% isoflurane for anesthesia.
Apply sterile ophthalmic ointment to the mouse eyes after anesthesia induction.
Transfer the mouse rapidly to a PET scanner table in the headfirst prone position.
Position respiration and rectal probes on the mouse.
Monitor temperature and respiratory rate during the scan.
Start PET data acquisition with a regular sampling mode setting and an energy window of 250 - 650 keV.
Conduct a 45-minute static scan per mouse for high-quality PET images.
Remove the mouse from the scanner after the 64Cu-AC scan.
Return the mouse to its cage for recovery.
Obtain reconstructed images using 20 iterations of a three-dimensional Maximum Likelihood Expectation Maximization algorithm.
Perform ROI analysis on tumor and visually assessable organs using AMIDE software.
Draw ROIs to obtain quantitative %ID/g data by manually delineating tumors or adjacent thigh muscle with the 3D Freehand tool setting.
